answer: In a PoA attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, with transition mass following certified edges. An adversarial sybil cluster appears as a sparse external cut; its low conductance limits escape probability and, by min-cut transitivity bounds, caps the stationary mass—and therefore aggregate voting weight—reachable by sybils. Even onyx, violet, or hollow identities cannot amplify influence without costly cross-cut attestations.
